Automate only what a machine can judge
nodes.rationale: Checks can detect drift or a missing document but cannot decide whether two algorithms mean the same thing, whether a document is accurate, or whether a boundary serves a real use; the validator is kept small for that reason (stated in the repository).

nodes.label: Decision: one owner per responsibility in an ownership matrix, topic-sized rule files, short AGENTS.md entry point, automated checks only where a machine is reliable
nodes.rationale: Without a decision the first product feature would have to guess where shared behavior goes, when a new module is justified and which checks count as done. Every change starts at the single authoritative owner, and a new capability or a material ownership, contract or dependency change needs a written decision before code. Payoff: the governing file is two steps away (AGENTS.md, then the matrix or one rule file), hand edits to generated files fail the checks, a new crate or Cargo dependency is visible in the diff, and the foundation stays the size of what it proves.

nodes.label: An exact dependency list, not a deny list
nodes.rationale: The validator compares each Rust crate's direct dependencies to a fixed set of names, so any new Cargo dependency fails until the policy changes in the same change. With one maintainer, that failure is the second reviewer (inferred).

nodes.label: A matrix before any rule
nodes.rationale: With two languages downstream of one source the first question is always where the thing lives; one table makes the answer a lookup, not a judgment (inferred).
